Hannah — thanks for coordinating. Uploaded my notes to the Drive and pasted the highlights below.

Summary bullets:
- Candidate is thoughtful and asks good clarifying questions; showed product awareness (liked the prompt about inference latency trade-offs).
- Struggled on one design subproblem (cache invalidation scenario) — gave a plausible but incomplete approach.
- Code portion was fine; small bug in concurrency handling but fixes were straightforward.
- Culture fit: collaborative, worked well with follow-ups.

Numeric:
- Technical: 3/5
- System design: 2/5 (concern)
- Communication: 4/5
- Overall: Yellow — OK for take-home but not a slam dunk. Recommend providing a more focused design rubric for the take-home to mitigate the cache question.

Notes in Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/rdw-hiring/EZhao/mina-notes.txt

Subject: Re: Scorecards: SDE Interview — Emily Zhao (round 1)

Thanks team — I pulled the recording and skimmed the code exercise. My read: solid culture fit, communicates clearly, but system design depth is borderline for the level we're hiring. Thoughts:

- I agree with Aditya that the candidate recovers well and shows good intuition.
- Mina's cache invalidation concern matters; the question we asked hits an area we care about for this role.
- I would be comfortable moving the candidate to a short, tightly scoped take-home that focuses on a small system-design + correctness checks (2-3 hours). If they do well, bring them back for a deeper design loop.

My scores (uploaded to compiled sheet):
- Technical: 3/5
- System design: 2/5
- Communication: 4/5
- Recommendation: Yellow — move to take-home with focused prompts

I propose we set the take-home deadline to 5 business days and include a sample rubric so graders know to prioritize the cache/invalidation section. If anyone objects to the take-home route, please say so here and we can discuss. Otherwise I'll draft the instructions and rubric after we collect the final votes.

— Marissa
Hiring Manager, Platform
Redwood Inference
